name: שְׁפַטְיָה
summary: Borne by David’s fifth son, born of Abital in Hebron; by one of the princes who heard Jeremiah foretell the city’s fall and asked the king to put him to death (Jer 38:1–4); by a son of king Jehoshaphat; by a Benjamite of the Haruphites who came to David at Ziklag; by the leader of Simeon under David; by Benjamite and Judahite forefathers of men in Jerusalem after the exile; and by two families of the return, one of them of Solomon’s servants. It is שָׁפַט “he has judged” followed by the divine name in its short form ‑יָה or ‑יָהוּ: “Yahweh has judged”, the same sentence as יְהוֹשָׁפָט with its parts the other way round, and one of the sons of Jehoshaphat bears it (2Ch 21:2).

evidence.note: “The fifth, שְׁפַטְיָה the son of Abital”, among David’s sons born in Hebron. So 1Ch 3:3.
“שְׁפַטְיָה son of Mattan … heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people.”
The princes ask that this man be put to death, for he weakens the hands of the men of war.
Among “the sons of יְהוֹשָׁפָט”: וּשְׁפַטְיָהוּ. The son bears his father’s name with its parts reversed.
“וּשְׁפַטְיָהוּ the Haruphite”, among those who came to David at Ziklag.
“For the Simeonites, שְׁפַטְיָהוּ son of Maacah.”
“Meshullam son of שְׁפַטְיָה son of Reuel”, a Benjamite in Jerusalem.
In the line of Athaiah of the sons of Perez: “son of שְׁפַטְיָה son of Mahalalel”.
“The sons of שְׁפַטְיָה, three hundred seventy and two.” So Neh 7:9; Ezr 8:8.
Among the sons of Solomon’s servants. So Neh 7:59.
“Judge me (שָׁפְטֵנִי), Yahweh, according to my righteousness”: Yahweh as the subject of the verb, as in the name.
The same kind of confession in a name: “God has judged me (דָּנַנִּי)”, so she called him Dan, with the neighbouring verb.

note: TIPNR keys the Haruphite Shephatiah@1Ch.12.5 (English numbering); the verse is 1Ch 12:6 in the Hebrew. 1Ch 3:3 is David’s son again. The families of Ezr 2:4 and 2:57 are named for a forefather, not a person in the text; TIPNR keys them as persons and they are tagged so.
